blocks.text: Lasso demonstrated the core embedded method idea using a linear model, coefficients driven to exactly zero during training. Tree-based selection applies that genuine same core idea, selection emerging naturally from training, to an entirely different kind of model, decision trees and ensembles, where feature importance emerges directly from how much each feature actually helps reduce error across every split.

This topic covers exactly how a decision tree chooses each split and records the resulting impurity reduction, how that reduction accumulates into a genuine, final importance score per feature, why ensembles like random forests produce a genuinely more stable importance estimate than a single tree, how to actually drop low importance features using SelectFromModel, and two real, honest limitations, a genuine bias toward high cardinality features, and diluted importance among genuinely correlated features.
1. How a Tree Chooses Each Split

blocks.alt: How a Tree Chooses Each Split
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443422377-233206890.png

At every genuine split point while a decision tree is being built, the algorithm considers every available feature and threshold, and chooses whichever combination genuinely reduces impurity the most, a measure of how mixed together the different target classes, or how spread out the different target values, currently are at that specific point in the tree. This genuine impurity reduction is recorded directly at the moment that split is actually made.

This mechanism, covered here at a conceptual level, is the genuine foundation the specific tree based algorithms covered later in the Classification and Regression Algorithms modules are actually built on, this topic focuses specifically on the byproduct that mechanism produces, a genuine, usable feature importance score.
2. Accumulating Importance Across Every Split
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443422378-496040182.png

A feature genuine final importance score is computed by summing up its impurity reduction across every single split where it was actually used, throughout the entire tree, and, for an ensemble like a random forest, across every individual tree in that ensemble as well. A feature used at many genuinely impactful splits accumulates a genuinely high importance score, while one rarely or never used for a useful split accumulates a genuinely low one.

This accumulation is genuinely what makes tree based importance a real, direct measure of how much a feature actually mattered during training, not an estimate computed separately or afterward, but a genuine, running tally kept throughout the actual learning process itself.
3. Why Ensembles Produce a More Stable Estimate

blocks.alt: Why Ensembles Produce a More Stable Estimate
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443422378-912518224.png

A genuine single decision tree, trained on one specific sample of data, can produce an importance estimate that shifts considerably if trained again on a slightly different sample, a real, honest instability. A random forest, training genuinely many trees on different random samples and feature subsets, averages importance across all of them, smoothing out that individual tree noise into a genuinely more stable, reliable estimate.

This is genuinely one of the real, practical reasons ensemble methods, covered in far more depth in the Ensemble Learning module later in this course, are so often preferred over a single decision tree specifically for feature importance work, not just for their genuine predictive accuracy.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: A single decision tree feature importance can genuinely shift noticeably between training runs on slightly different data. An ensemble genuine averaging across many trees is what makes this importance estimate trustworthy enough to act on.

blocks.text: 4. A Worked Example
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443422379-849014915.png
Using scikit-learn SelectFromModel with a trained random forest shows tree-based selection actually removing low importance features directly, not just ranking them.

code.content:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectFromModel
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "square_feet": [900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2100, 2400],
    "bedrooms": [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5],
    "shoe_size_unrelated": [8, 9, 7, 10, 8, 9],
})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1])

model = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42)
selector = SelectFromModel(model, threshold="median")
selector.fit(X, y)

print("Selected features:", X.columns[selector.get_support()].tolist())

blocks.text: SelectFromModel genuinely trains the random forest once internally, reads its feature_importances_ directly, and keeps only the features genuinely scoring above the median importance threshold, correctly dropping shoe_size_unrelated in this small, deliberately constructed example.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Try threshold values like "median" or "mean" in SelectFromModel as a genuinely sensible starting point, before tuning to a specific numeric cutoff based on real, observed importance scores.

blocks.text: 5. A Real, Known Limitation: Bias Toward High Cardinality Features

blocks.alt: A Real, Known Limitation: Bias Toward High Cardinality Features
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443422715-897053580.png

A genuinely high cardinality numeric feature, one with many unique values, gets genuinely more opportunities to be chosen as a good split point simply because it offers more possible threshold values to try, which can produce a genuinely inflated importance score that does not necessarily reflect real, meaningful predictive power. This is a genuine, well documented bias in impurity based importance specifically, not a hypothetical edge case.

This real limitation is worth taking seriously, a feature like a near unique row identifier can sometimes receive a suspiciously high importance score purely due to this cardinality effect, not because it genuinely helps predict the target at all, exactly the kind of concern the next, final topic in this module addresses directly.

blocks.text: 6. A Second Real Limitation: Diluted Importance Among Correlated Features

blocks.alt: A Second Real Limitation: Diluted Importance Among Correlated Features
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443422717-972687694.png

When two features are genuinely highly correlated with each other, exactly the redundancy first covered back in Feature Relationships, a tree can genuinely use either one interchangeably at different splits, since they carry largely the genuine same information. This splits their combined, real importance across both features individually, making each one look genuinely less important on its own than their true, combined contribution actually deserves.

This is a genuinely real, practical trap, two genuinely important, correlated features can each individually score low enough to be genuinely, mistakenly dropped, even though together they carry real, meaningful signal, exactly the kind of redundancy worth checking for directly using the correlation techniques covered earlier in this module before trusting importance scores in isolation.

blocks.text: 7. Applying This to Regression as Well

blocks.alt: Applying This to Regression as Well
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443422717-225633400.png

Everything covered in this topic applies genuinely identically to regression trees, the only real difference is the impurity measure itself, classification trees genuinely use something like Gini impurity or entropy, while regression trees genuinely use variance reduction instead, how much a split reduces the spread of target values within each resulting group.

The underlying importance accumulation mechanism, and both real limitations covered above, genuinely apply the exact same way regardless of whether the specific problem is a classification or a regression one.
8. Tree-Based Selection Versus What Comes Next

Lasso and Tree-Based Selection together cover two genuinely different, real embedded mechanisms, coefficients driven to zero for linear models, and impurity reduction accumulated across splits for tree based ones. Both, though, are genuinely specific to their own particular model family, and tree based importance specifically carries the two real limitations just covered.

The next and final topic in this module, Feature Importance, ties every one of these ideas together into one genuine, general framework, and introduces permutation importance, a genuinely model agnostic technique that directly addresses both real limitations covered in this topic.

items: Tree based selection derives feature importance from how much each feature reduces impurity across every split.
Importance accumulates across every split a feature is used in, and across every tree in an ensemble.
Random forests genuinely average importance across many trees, producing a more stable estimate than one tree.
SelectFromModel genuinely drops features below a chosen importance threshold, directly from a trained tree model.
Impurity based importance genuinely carries a real bias toward high cardinality numeric features.
Genuinely correlated features can dilute each other apparent importance, even when jointly important together.
